title: Document model
body: A document is one JSON file in the sources folder. The id is the file name without the extension: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen. Folder names follow the same rules, and the reserved Windows names are rejected. ^fsh5

The built-in schema requires only `title`. The reserved fields are `title`, `kind`, `status`, `parent`, `order`, `tags`, `body`, `notes`, `hidden`, `docIgnore` and `$comments`. Every other field is free and holds prose. `order` is a number that sorts a document among its siblings. ^eqdv
The checks are listed in [[rules@masz]] and the generated pages in [[rendering@67mw]]. ^u4pc
typing: Every document has a `kind`, and the folder of schemas holds `<kind>.json` for it. A document without a kind, or with a kind that has no schema, is reported as DOC109, a core rule that cannot be switched off. ^dfgy

A kind schema must set a boolean `additionalProperties` at the top level: `true` makes the kind flexible, `false` makes it strict. Without it the schema does not load and docc exits with code 2. For a strict kind docc checks the field names itself: the allowed names are the reserved fields, the top-level `properties` and the `properties` of the top-level `allOf` branches and of local `$ref` targets; names under `if` and `then` are not counted. An unknown field is DOC106 with the message `unknown field X` and a suggestion of the closest allowed name. ^e9ea
The kind schema sees the whole document, reserved fields included, so it can require `parent` or limit the values of `status`. ^c4ya

`"x-docc-target": ["goal"]` on a property, `parent` included, limits the kinds of the documents its references point to; a reference to another kind is DOC214. `"x-docc-covered": true` at the top level of a kind schema means that every visible document of the kind needs a `docc:` tag in code, otherwise DOC403 warns when `trace.scan` is set; each of its blocks also needs a tag that names it, `id#^code`, otherwise DOC404 warns. On a property it asks that only for the blocks of that field; when any property is marked, the top-level mark no longer covers the other fields. A tag on the whole document or on a field covers no block: it does not say which code implements which paragraph. ^7wum
references: Inside any string, `[[id]]` links to a document and `[[id#field]]` links to one of its fields. Both are checked like `parent`. A reference in the text is the link: it joins two documents in the graph and puts the source under Referenced by on the target page; there is no separate list of links. References inside `notes` are checked but give no reachability. Code blocks and inline code are ignored. ^wr5g
A long text is an array of paragraphs, one per line of the file. The rules are applied to each element on its own. ^793y

A reference can name a section inside a field, `[[id#field/section@hash]]`, or a block by its code, `[[id#^k7f2@hash]]` (a code is found in any case). DOC312 checks the whole path and reports an unknown field, section or code. ^5rxb
block_anchors: Every text block (a paragraph, a list item, the text of a field or section) ends with a space and a permanent code `^k7f2`: four signs of `23456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz`, unique in the project, shown to readers upper case. `docc build` gives one to a block without it; nobody writes or changes a code by hand, and a block keeps its code when it moves. `[[id#^k7f2@hash]]` links to that block and `{{id#^k7f2}}` includes it without the code. A Markdown page gets an HTML anchor before a block that some link points to; the HTML file shows the code with buttons to copy a link and the code. ^9dmp

A block without a code, or ending in a named anchor of the old format, is DOC216; a code on two blocks of the project (a copied paragraph), or equal to the anchor of a field or section heading of the page, is DOC212, which names both places. Both are core rules. ^gw3b
change_tracking: Every link carries the version hash of its target: `[[id@hash]]`, `[[id#field@hash]]`, `[[id#^code@hash]]`, and every target of a `docc:` tag in code the same. The hash is four signs from SHA-256 of the target; a missing or old hash is DOC209, a core error. Code tags end with the fingerprint of their code: `~xxxx` on the tag of a file for its lines outside regions, on `docc:begin` for the lines of the region; a missing or old one is DOC402, a core error. ^rrbx

The hash covers only what the link points to: a block hashes its text, a field or section its value, and a whole document is hashed without `notes`, `docIgnore`, `hidden`, `order`, `parent` and `$comments`, so a reader's comment breaks no link. Block codes and the hashes inside links are left out of every hash, so two documents that link each other never loop. A fingerprint leaves out the hashes and fingerprints of `docc:` lines. ^mfzz

When a target changes, DOC209 on every link to it shows what changed (the old version found in the Git history by its hash, or the text now) and the hash it has now: read it, check that the linking place still agrees, then write that hash by hand. When code changes, DOC402 lists the targets with their text and the fingerprint the code has now: check the code against them, then write it by hand. No command does this in bulk. ^zkpc
`docc migrate` moves a project of the old format, which kept the hashes in `docc.lock`, to hashes in the links, once; until then docc refuses the project. ^a8d8
hidden_material: `notes` are for agents and never reach the Markdown. ^hphn
A document with `hidden` set to `true` is checked like any other, gets no page and cannot be linked from a visible document. ^68v4
The include `{{id#field}}`, `{{id#field/section}}` or `{{id#^name}}` is replaced at build time by the text it names, so a fact is stored once. ^zvgy
suppression: `docIgnore` lists entries with a rule (its name, such as text/forbidden-words), a mandatory reason and an optional JSON pointer path. Core rules cannot be suppressed or switched off. An entry that suppresses nothing is reported as DOC901. ^8zkf
sections: A free field can hold named sections: an object with the member `"$sections": true`, whose other keys are section titles. A value is text, an array of paragraphs, a list object or another set of sections. It is rendered as a second level heading for the field, third level for a section, and so on up to the sixth, in file order. A section without text keeps its heading, so a link to it has a target. ^bmtf
An object without the marker is rendered as a bullet list. The marker means nothing outside the value of a field or a section. ^d98j

A section is linked with `[[id#field/section]]`; the link text is the section title, not the title of the document. A section is included with `{{id#field/section}}`; the path is matched against the keys, so a key may contain a slash. The anchor comes from the heading like the anchor of a field; equal anchors on one page are numbered -1, -2 in page order. Text rules and `docIgnore` paths treat sections like fields. A kind schema describes the marker as `"properties": {"$sections": {"const": true}}`. ^7fy7
form_fields: An item of an array of paragraphs (`body`, a free field or a section) can be a form field: `{"$input": "radio", "id": "export", "label": "Export to Excel?", "options": ["Yes", "No"]}`. `$input` is `text` (a text box), `radio` (one choice of two or more options) or `checkbox` (any choices of one or more options); the id is unique in the document and the answers are kept by it; `label` is the question; a text box has no options; no other keys are allowed. A radio or checkbox field also takes an own answer, a text that is none of its options: radio one option or one own text, checkbox the options ticked and at most one own text. DOC112 reports an answer with no value, a blank value or a value given twice, and an answer to the field as it reads now that the field cannot take; an answer to an earlier version of the question is not checked against the field. `docc comments apply` checks the same on add and edit and trims the values that are not options, as the HTML file does. DOC111 reports a malformed field and a field outside an array of paragraphs. ^dh85

The author writes the fields in the sources, by hand or through an agent; readers answer them in the HTML file ([[rendering@67mw]]). The Markdown output leaves them out. In the history a field is a block of its own, so the paragraphs around it keep theirs. Text rules read only the question and the options. The built-in schema allows a field in `body`; a free field holding one needs a kind schema that allows the object. ^znmy
comments: The top-level member `$comments` holds the readers' comments of the document as a flat list: `[{"id", "at", "quote", "fragment"?, "prefix"?, "suffix"?, "text", "author", "email"?, "created", "edited"?}]`. `id` is unique in the project (docc gives `c-` and ten characters of a-z and 2-7), `at` is the JSON Pointer of a block the reader sees on the page (never notes, `docIgnore`, `hidden`, the title or `$comments`), `quote` the source text of that block when the comment was written (docc fills it from the block, whatever the caller gives), `fragment`, `prefix` and `suffix` the selected words and a few characters around them, `author` a name (it may be empty), `created` an RFC 3339 time and `edited` the RFC 3339 time of the last edit of the text or the answer (docc comments apply edit sets it; add does not). An answer to a form field has `input` (the field id) and `answer` (an array of strings) instead of `text`, and its `at` points at the field. ^mjtp

There are no statuses and no replies: a handled comment is deleted in the same commit as the fix, and a note meant only for agents goes into `notes`. The member is allowed under every kind like `title`, even by a strict kind schema; text rules do not read it, it is no section of the page and no block of the history, and the version hash of a whole document leaves it out. Only docc writes it, with `docc comments apply` ([[commands@nmzt]]). DOC112 reports a malformed item or an id used twice in the project; DOC215 warns when a comment lost its place: no block has the code in `at` (the block was deleted), the selected words are gone from the block, or the answered field is not there. ^wp9d
